source_text.ISS-0936: Issue ISS-0936 (local record docs/issues/ISS-0936.yaml, queue_ref Q-919, queue task 919, GH#2070; record may not yet be on this branch - PR #2071): scripts/uat_preflight.sh's qa-uat-env credential protocol (fetch_credential, ~line 290) expects the credential source's `token <user>` to print a line `Token: <jwt>`, but ai-dala-infra's qa-uat-env.sh `token <user>` prints a BARE JWT, so every actor login reports NO_PASSWORD. Fix: make fetch_credential accept a bare JWT line (three dot-separated base64url segments) as well as the `Token:` form. Add/adjust tests per project's existing preflight tests (none found under test/ -- TEST-DESIGNER decides a minimal in-repo test shape). Also update the script's header docs (qa-uat-env protocol paragraph) and scripts/README.md if they state the Token: form.

task.description: WF-03 Step 2b re-validation after rework 1 (prior FAIL in step-02b-code-design-validator.json listed 6 gaps: flag names, assertion substrings, T7 undecided, fixture shape, JWT length 49, Q2). Re-read the revised lib/letflow/design/iss0936-uat-preflight-bare-jwt.md and independently verify each gap is closed AND that the pinned substrings/flags actually match the script's real output formats (read scripts/uat_preflight.sh; you may sanity-run the script with a fake source if useful, using tmp files outside the repo). result.summary: FAIL (2 new defects, prior 6 gaps all closed). Prior gaps verified closed against scripts/uat_preflight.sh: G1 flags named and match argparse lines 112-114; G2 substrings match real output (line 532 `login failed: <aid>(<STATE>)` in DETAIL; line 636 `credential validity   : <aid>@<realm>=<STATE>` with 3 spaces and `none checked` fallback; realm derives to swiftroute via realms_for); G3 T7 decided IN with stub spec; G4 fixture pinned, both parse_scenario paths (yaml and regex fallback, lines 156-175) yield id/company_id/actors; G5 JWT length 49 verified (20+15+12+2); G6/Q2 resolved. However re-verification against the script found two new defects that block a clean build.
issues: N1 (factual error + hermeticity, design sec 6.2 T7 and Base URL bullets): the design claims the stub server receives the three /realms/<slug>/.well-known/openid-configuration GETs and that the catch-all 200 covers them. In the script (line 132) idp defaults to 'https://auth.' + host, i.e. https://auth.127.0.0.1 for base http://127.0.0.1:<port>, and the realm GETs (lines 384-386) go to idp, NOT base. So they never reach the stub; there are also only TWO slugs (swiftroute, bpm-default), not three. Consequence: every test T1-T7 makes real DNS/HTTPS attempts to auth.127.0.0.1 (non-hermetic, possibly slow in CI; each call has 15s timeout). Fix: add `--idp-url <base URL>` (argparse line 113 supports it) to the pinned command line for all tests (T1-T6 http://127.0.0.1:9, T7 the stub URL), and correct the T7 route list to: /health, two realm well-known paths via the stub (now that idp=base), /api/v1/me/modules, /api/v1/tasks/inbox.

N2 (formatting defect making the spec ambiguous, design lines 159-161): the T5 row contains two literal blank lines inside the cell (`followed by CRLF (` newline newline `) line ending`), which splits the markdown table; T5 and T6/T7 rows no longer render as table rows and the CRLF payload is unreadable. Replace with an escaped form in the cell, e.g. `@jwt` followed by `\r\n`, and state how the fake source emits it (printf '%s\r\n'). Also note for accuracy: the script's subprocess.run uses text=True (universal newlines, line 264) so CR is normalized before R1 is reached; T5 therefore guards end-to-end behavior, not R1 specifically. State that or drop the claim that T5 exercises the strip.

N3 (minor, sec 6.1/Q2): 'the test fails loudly with a message telling the developer to set UAT_PF_BASH' does not say how a WSL-stub bash is detected. Pin the mechanism (e.g. if the run output contains neither 'UAT PREFLIGHT' header nor ... assert with a failure message naming UAT_PF_BASH), or state that the ordinary assertion failure message must include that hint.
